statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
be an object such that there exists a locally bounded complex
$\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ of finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
representing $E$. Then the characteristic-class constructions for locally bounded complexes, defined by alternating formal Chern-class products and alternating power-sum/character sums
$$
c(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in \prod\nolimits_{p \geq 0} A^p(X),\quad
ch(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in
\prod\nolimits_{p \geq 0} A^p(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q},\quad
P_p(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in A^p(X)
$$
are independent of the choice of the complex $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chern-classes-defined}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
be a perfect object. If one of the following conditions hold, then
the Chern classes of $E$ are defined:
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists an envelope $f : Y \to X$ such that $Lf^*E$
is isomorphic in $D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ to a locally bounded complex of finite
locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules,
\item $E$ can be represented by a bounded complex of finite locally
free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules,
\item the irreducible components of $X$ are quasi-compact,
\item $X$ is quasi-compact,
\item there exists a morphism $X \to X'$ of schemes locally of finite type
over $S$ such that $E$ is the pullback of a perfect object $E'$ on $X'$
whose chern classes are defined, or
\item add more here.
\end{enumerate}

Both assertions and the definability antecedent are preserved.

\label{lemma-additivity-on-perfect}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Let
$$
E_1 \to E_2 \to E_3 \to E_1[1]
$$
be a distinguished triangle of perfect objects in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
If one of the following conditions holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists an envelope $f : Y \to X$ such that
$Lf^*E_1 \to Lf^*E_2$ can be represented by a map of locally
bounded complexes of finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules,
\item $E_1 \to E_2$ can be represented be a map of locally bounded complexes
of finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules,
\item the irreducible components of $X$ are quasi-compact,
\item $X$ is quasi-compact, or
\item add more here,
\end{enumerate}
then the Chern classes of $E_1$, $E_2$, $E_3$ are defined and we have
$c(E_2) = c(E_1) c(E_3)$, $ch(E_2) = ch(E_1) + ch(E_3)$, and
$P_p(E_2) = P_p(E_1) + P_p(E_3)$.

\label{lemma-chern-class-perfect-tensor-invertible}
In Situation \ref{situation-setup} let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $E$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ whose Chern classes
are defined.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then
$$
c_i(E \otimes \mathcal{L}) =
\sum\nolimits_{j = 0}^i
\binom{r - i + j}{j} c_{i - j}(E) c_1(\mathcal{L})^j
$$
provided $E$ has constant rank $r \in \mathbf{Z}$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-chern-classes-perfect-tensor-product}
In Situation \ref{situation-setup} let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $E$ and $F$ be perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ whose Chern classes
are defined. Then we have
$$
c_1(E \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} F) =
r(E) c_1(\mathcal{F}) + r(F) c_1(\mathcal{E})
$$
and for $c_2(E \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} F)$ we have the expression
$$
r(E) c_2(F) + r(F) c_2(E) + {r(E) \choose 2} c_1(F)^2 +
(r(E)r(F) - 1) c_1(F)c_1(E) + {r(F) \choose 2} c_1(E)^2
$$
and so on for higher Chern classes in $A^*(X)$. Similarly, we have
$ch(E \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} F) = ch(E) ch(F)$
in $A^*(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q}$. More precisely, we have
$$
P_p(E \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} F) = \sum\nolimits_{p_1 + p_2 = p}
{p \choose p_1} P_{p_1}(E) P_{p_2}(F)
$$
in $A^p(X)$.
